affiliations.occupation: Artist, sculptor, or teacher of art
affiliations.date_precision: The official Army-entry record carries civilian occupation code 004 on 25 February 1942. NARA's official list defines the grouped code as artists, sculptors, and teachers of art and names no employer.
affiliations.research_notes: The exact private identifier confirms the Army-entry row. The code does not distinguish artist, sculptor, or art teacher, and the project does not infer an employer.

affiliations.date_precision: The official Army-entry record carries civilian occupation code 932 on 20 November 1942. NARA's official list defines the grouped code as construction occupations not elsewhere classified and names no employer.
affiliations.research_notes: The exact private identifier confirms the Army-entry row. The grouped code supplies no specific trade, workplace, or employer.

claims.claim_text: The indexed Technician Fifth Grade Carl J. Beato is confirmed as the Army entrant represented by the exact-name and private-identifier match in the official merged file.
claims.evidence_paraphrase: The exact name and private service identifier match across the OSS index and official Army-entry file; the full identifier is withheld.
claims.identity_match_assessment: Confirmed by the exact full name, exact private identifier, and compatible enlisted Army status.
claims.temporal_assessment: The official record dates Army entry to 25 February 1942; the OSS index does not establish the later transfer chronology.
claims.match_notes: The official file records Private at Army entry; the later index rank of Technician Fifth Grade is chronologically compatible. The decisive identifier remains private.

claims.claim_text: At Army entry in February 1942, Carl J. Beato's civilian occupation code represented artist, sculptor, or art-teacher work.
claims.evidence_excerpt: 004. Artists, sculptors, and teachers of art
claims.evidence_paraphrase: The exact-matched Army-entry row carries code 004; NARA's official list defines a three-occupation group and names no employer.
claims.identity_match_assessment: The exact private-identifier match confirms that the Army-entry row belongs to the indexed person.
claims.temporal_assessment: Strongly date-bounded to Army entry on 25 February 1942, but not proven to be his final civilian role before OSS.
claims.match_notes: Published as the complete occupation group. No particular occupation or employer is selected without further evidence.

claims.claim_text: The indexed French Second Lieutenant Andre Beau is a high-confidence match to the André Beau named in a NARA-published history of OSS work in France.
claims.evidence_excerpt: The person in charge of falsifying papers for the organization, André Beau, printed tiny pamphlets for them
claims.evidence_paraphrase: A NARA-published conference history names André Beau in the operational context of a French OSS network.
claims.identity_match_assessment: High confidence from the rare exact name, the index's French note, the indexed military rank, and a specific independent OSS-in-France context; no private identifier is available for confirmation.
claims.temporal_assessment: The passage concerns wartime OSS activity and establishes identity context only; it does not document pre-OSS employment.
claims.match_notes: The identity is not promoted to confirmed because the secondary institutional history supplies no service number or direct personnel-file linkage. No employment claim is derived from the OSS role.

person_updates.identity_evidence: The visually verified index supplies Gladys M. Beason, grade CPC-3, and Box 44 but no private identifier. Exact-name official, CIA, Library of Congress, employment, occupation, obituary, newspaper, and institutional searches produced no candidate meeting the identity rule.
person_updates.next_action: Review Box 44 for Gladys M. Beason's full middle and possible married names, CPC-3 duties, occupation, employer, and recruitment chronology. No reliable pre-OSS employer has yet been identified in the accessible sources reviewed.

person_updates.identity_evidence: The index supplies John W. Beaston Jr., a private identifier, and Box 44. An official Army-file exact-name-and-suffix row had a different private identifier and a 1946 entry date and was rejected; no defensible identity or employer remained.
person_updates.next_action: Review Box 44 to resolve John W. Beaston Jr.'s service record, branch, birth data, occupation, employer, and chronology; do not merge the different-identifier Army namesake. No reliable pre-OSS employer has yet been identified in the accessible sources reviewed.

person_updates.next_action: Review Box 44 and the original Army card to distinguish artist, sculptor, or art teacher, identify the employer if any, and establish the OSS transition. No reliable pre-OSS employer has yet been identified in the accessible sources reviewed.

person_updates.identity_evidence: The index identifies Andre Beau as a French Second Lieutenant. A NARA-published OSS history independently names Andre Beau in a specific French OSS network context. The rare exact name, French context, and direct OSS association support high confidence but no private identifier confirms the match.
person_updates.next_action: Review Box 44 and French military or resistance records to confirm the identity and establish pre-OSS occupation, employer or unit, and chronology. The documented OSS task is not treated as pre-OSS employment. No reliable pre-OSS employer has yet been identified in the accessible sources reviewed.
